requirements.text: A source publishes a lifecycle policy: how long a leaving public name keeps working and how its removal date is computed. A name leaves on a date the policy gives, never undated.
requirements.guidance: 1.0.0 id one-version-line. Framework: one long version line and a calendar, per contracts/lifecycle-policy.json. A semver source may bind removal to its next major; a mirror copies the dates of the original source.

requirements.text: A public name leaves in two stages. Compat: it still works, through an alias or a shim, and its replacement is documented. Removed: it is gone. There is no third, undated state.
Every change that asks a consumer to change anything is recorded in a machine-readable change journal. A change without a record is not released.

A record names each old form and what to write instead, the kind of change from the list of the profile, whether the rewrite is mechanical (a rewrite of the profile, manual or none) and, when it is not, an instruction and a before/after example a person or an AI can apply.
requirements.guidance: Framework kinds: attribute, value, event, class, token, utility, option, property, component, behaviour, format, global. Templates kinds: template, parameter, option, field, clause, party.

requirements.text: A record carries the date it was deprecated and the date it is removed on, computed by the policy.
The journal is append-only. A record is never deleted; a removed name stays as a tombstone, so a consumer on any older release can still be upgraded by reading it.
The journal is chronological, so it is also the history of the public surface, readable without the commit log.
Every compatibility the source keeps (an alias, a shim, an accepted old value) has a record; one found without a record fails the gate.
On or after its removal date a compat record is removed from the source and marked removed; a compat record past its date fails the gate.
A record may be extended once, by at most the extension period of the policy, with a reason that names the consumer still depending on the name and the date it migrates.
Compatibility is resolved in shared places, not scattered through the content, so removing it touches one place.
A consumer can find out that it still uses a compat name without reading the journal by hand: a runtime note, a build warning, a reconcile status.
requirements.guidance: 1.0.0 id runtime-notes-use. Framework profile: must; a page that uses a legacy name gets it noted at runtime, readable as SF.deprecations.list(); silent by default, console warnings opt-in.

requirements.text: Upgrading a consumer reads the journal: a tool finds every old form, rewrites the mechanical ones and lists the rest with their instruction. No upgrade depends on reading prose.
requirements.guidance: Framework: scripts/sf-upgrade.mjs. Templates: saved answer sets and document passports are migrated by the journal.

requirements.text: Before a removal the known consumers are scanned with the upgrade tool and migrated, so a removal breaks nobody who could have been told. Under simai.linkage the known consumers are those whose usage records name the unit; their reconcile shows former-name with the removal date.
The policy, the journal and how to upgrade with it are published for readers, and each record's replacement appears where the unit is documented.
The gate holds the journal's form, the policy's dates, the append-only rule and the compat coverage; the profile adds its own checks.
requirements.guidance: Framework: tests/change-lifecycle.contract.test.mjs and the browser check of the runtime note.

requirements.text: A mirror (simai.linkage mirror-source) records the changes of the original source in its own journal with the original dates and act. no-compat-without-record, remove-on-date and extension-once-with-reason do not apply to it, because it neither keeps the compat nor decides the dates. upgrade-from-the-journal is met by reconcile finding every affected place; the rewrite is manual, applied by a person from the instruction of the record.
requirements.guidance: Does not apply to the Framework profile.
